highLevelPlan: Wire the toolbar affordances that are already mounted but inert: RectifyWindow.kt line 304 composes `AppButton(text = "Resolve & Send", onClick = {}, shortcut = "⌘↵", enabled = false)` and the `CounterBadge`/`Clear` slots are live. FR-16/AC-17 is mostly a wiring job, not new UI.

Add a send state machine to MirrorContract/MirrorViewModel: one `MirrorIntent.ResolveAndSend`, one `SendPhase` value in `MirrorUiState`, reusing the existing `canResumeLive`/`stagedCount` precedent for derived guards (FR-16, FR-18, AC-20).

Capture what the envelope needs but F-6 never kept: the frozen frame's RAW PNG bytes (`MirrorFrame.bytes`, discarded today after `decodePng`) and the raw uiautomator dump text (discarded today by `HierarchySnapshotMapper`). Both are gaps, not assembly work (FR-57, AC-18).

Add `:data-handoff-api` — a convention-plugin library module holding the `@Serializable` envelope (carrying `version` from F-6's `PAYLOAD_FORMAT_VERSION`) and the publish/read seam, with the desktop-only implementation bound through the `expect fun Module.provideX()` pattern `data-device-impl` already uses (FR-57, NFR-12, NFR-15, AC-32).

Add `:mcp-application` — a second plain-JVM `main()` speaking line-delimited JSON-RPC over stdin/stdout, exposing exactly one tool, `get_latest_annotation`, that reads the published slot (FR-56, AC-18, AC-81, NFR-4).

Render the send status sequence and the completion toast from already-shipped kit components (`StatusLine`/`StatusStep`, `CounterBadge`, `StackedSnackbarHost`), and route the toast's `Open session` clipboard copy through the window layer the way `CommandBlock.onCopy` already demands (FR-18, FR-58, AC-19).

Close the loop on success — resume live mirroring, reset the counter — and on failure leave the frozen frame and staged batch untouched so the same batch can be retried (FR-19, AC-20, AC-21, AS-31, SC-25).
data.proposedArchitecture:
Three seams, one of which is genuinely new.

**1. The publication seam (the crux).** The MCP server is a process Claude Code spawns via its own MCP config; Rectify is a different process the user launched. An in-memory Kotlin interface cannot bridge them, so the handoff needs an OS mechanism. Recommended: a **single-slot atomic file drop** under the app data dir — `~/.rectify/handoff/latest.json`, written as `latest.json.tmp` then `Files.move(..., ATOMIC_MOVE, REPLACE_EXISTING)`. One file, one rename, no lock, no partial read, no reader/writer handshake. The MCP server re-reads the slot on every `get_latest_annotation` call, which makes AC-81's idempotent 'latest' semantics a property of the storage rather than code someone has to write, and makes the payload survive Rectify not being running at tool-call time.

On the PRD's 'no file fallback transport': I read that as a statement about the **transport to the agent** — the agent must call an MCP tool, never be pointed at a directory of PNGs — and not about intra-machine plumbing between two local processes. FR-17's own wording ('publish it so a locally running Claude Code agent can retrieve it by calling a single MCP tool') is consistent with that reading: the contract is the tool call, the slot is private implementation behind it. The agent never learns the path. This is the single most likely thing in this document to be wrong; the alternative (`alternatives[1]`, an AF_UNIX socket) is scored honestly rather than dismissed.

**2. The envelope.** New module `:data-handoff-api` (`library` convention plugin, kotlinx-serialization — already cataloged, no new dependency). `source/envelope/AnnotationEnvelope.kt` is a `@Serializable` data class whose FIRST field is `version: Int`, defaulted from F-6's const — this is how AC-32/NFR-12 get satisfied without touching F-6's assembly at all. `PAYLOAD_FORMAT_VERSION` is `internal` to `presentation-feature-mirror/core/payload`; it stays there and stays internal, and the mirror-side publisher (the only code that can see it) passes it in as the constructor argument. Nothing in F-6 moves, nothing in F-6 is re-exported, and the one const keeps exactly one owner. `source/handoff/AnnotationHandoff.kt` declares `publish(envelope)`; `AnnotationHandoffReader.latest()` is the read side the server uses. Both are plain `commonMain` interfaces with a `desktopMain` file-backed implementation bound by `internal expect fun Module.provideAnnotationHandoff()` — a verbatim copy of `data-device-impl`'s `provideDeviceSources()` shape, including the Android/iOS `Unsupported*` actual that throws, which is how every target keeps linking under NFR-10/platform-coverage.md.

**3. The server process.** New module `:mcp-application`, plain JVM (`kotlin("jvm")` + `application`), depending on `:data-handoff-api` only — no Compose, no Koin graph, no Skiko. Its `main()` is a read-line loop over `System.in`: parse a JSON-RPC request with `kotlinx.serialization.json`, answer `initialize`, `tools/list` (one entry) and `tools/call` for `get_latest_annotation`, write one JSON object per line to `System.out`, and send everything diagnostic to `System.err` (a stray `println` on stdout corrupts the protocol — that is the single rule this module lives by). A hand-rolled JSON-RPC envelope is the right call here precisely because kotlinx-serialization already does the hard half: the framing is `readLine()`/`println`, and the remaining surface is three method names. Pulling in an MCP SDK or a ktor-server entry to avoid ~120 lines would be the larger decision, not the smaller one.

**Second entry point, stated plainly.** This repo has exactly one process entry point today (`:desktop-application`'s `Main.kt`). `:mcp-application` is a second one. It does not break the existing packaging story, because there isn't much of one to break — `compose.desktop.application { mainClass }` is the only packaging config present and `nativeDistributions {}` is not configured (per desktop-application/CLAUDE.md), so no installer currently bundles anything that a second module would have to be squeezed into. What it does add is a launch artefact the user's `.mcp.json` must name: `:mcp-application:installDist` produces `build/install/mcp-application/bin/mcp-application`, which is a stable path a config entry can point at. Convention plugins model KMP modules only and therefore model neither of these two — but `:desktop-application` already set that precedent deliberately and documented it, so this is an existing deviation extended by one, not a new class of exception. It is still listed under `gaps`.

**UI side.** No new design-system component is needed. `StatusLine` + `StatusStep`/`StatusStepState` already ships the exact four-step pipeline AND the exact failure variant — its own `@Preview` renders `Streaming › Frozen › Dumping hierarchy › Sent` with `trailing = "live"` and `Stream dropped (Error) › Frozen › …` with `trailing = "failed"`. The projection from `SendPhase` to `List<StatusStep>` is a pure function in `core/send/`, which is what makes AC-19's ordering testable in `commonTest` under this repo's no-Compose-UI-test-harness constraint. `CounterBadge` already has a `Sent` state; `AppButton` already has `busy` (which implies disabled, covering AC-20); `StackedSnackbarHost` hosts the toast; the `Open session` clipboard copy is passed up to `RectifyWindow` as a callback, following `CommandBlock`'s documented rule that copying belongs to the host because Compose's `ClipboardManager` is deprecated in this version.

components.name: :data-handoff-api (new library module)
components.responsibility: Owns the wire contract both processes compile against: `source/envelope/AnnotationEnvelope` (@Serializable, `version` first field — AC-32/NFR-12), `source/handoff/AnnotationHandoff` (publish) and `AnnotationHandoffReader` (read). `core/` holds the internal atomic-write/slot-path plumbing (desktopMain). `library` convention plugin, kotlinx-serialization only (NFR-15).

components.name: FileSlotAnnotationHandoff (desktopMain, internal)
components.responsibility: The only implementation of both interfaces. Writes `latest.json.tmp` + `Files.move(ATOMIC_MOVE, REPLACE_EXISTING)` into `~/.rectify/handoff/`; reads the slot whole on each call. Single slot by design: 'latest' is the whole contract (AC-81). `ponytail:` single slot, add a ring buffer only when F-9 history needs one.

components.name: UnsupportedAnnotationHandoff (androidMain/iosMain)
components.responsibility: The Android/iOS actual of `provideAnnotationHandoff()` — throws on publish. Mirrors `UnsupportedDeviceSources` exactly, so every target still links while the feature stays desktop-only (platform-coverage.md, NFR-10).

components.name: :mcp-application (new plain-JVM module)
components.responsibility: `main()` #2. Line-delimited JSON-RPC over stdin/stdout: `initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call` → `get_latest_annotation` returning the last published envelope. Depends on `:data-handoff-api` only. stdout carries protocol frames exclusively; every log line goes to stderr (FR-56, AC-18, AC-81, NFR-4).

components.name: presentation-feature-mirror/core/send/ (new, internal)
components.responsibility: Pure functions the send path is proved by: `sendSteps(phase): List<StatusStep>` (AC-19 ordering + the `Stream dropped` failure variant), `canSend(state): Boolean` (AC-17/AC-20), `toastLabel(count, seconds)` (the `Sent N annotations to Claude Code · frame + hierarchy · <time>s` machine string). Same precedent as `core/payload`'s `hasPayload`/`hierarchyOutlineDisplay` — lifted out of composables so `commonTest` can reach them.

components.name: presentation-feature-mirror/core/send/EnvelopeAssembly (internal)
components.responsibility: Builds `AnnotationEnvelope` from the frozen frame, the retained raw PNG bytes, the crop PNGs, the raw hierarchy dump, `buildPrompt(...)`/`promptOverride`, and `PAYLOAD_FORMAT_VERSION`. Reuses F-6's `buildPrompt` and `cropWindow` rather than re-deriving either.

components.name: MirrorViewModel send handler
components.responsibility: Handles `MirrorIntent.ResolveAndSend`: guards on `canSend`, drives `SendPhase` through Frozen → DumpingHierarchy → Sent, calls `AnnotationHandoff.publish`, measures elapsed with `TimeSource.Monotonic`, then on success posts the toast side effect, resumes live and clears the batch (FR-19/AC-21); on failure sets the failed phase and leaves `frozen` untouched (AS-31/AC-20/SC-25).

components.name: MirrorViewModel.frozenFrameBytes (new StateFlow)
components.responsibility: A fourth `StateFlow` beside `frame`/`frozenFrame`/`frozenHierarchy`, holding the frozen frame's ORIGINAL `MirrorFrame.bytes`. Avoids re-encoding the full screenshot entirely: `adb screencap -p` already hands over PNG, the ViewModel just throws it away after `decodePng` today. Same no-pixels-in-reduced-state rule as the three flows already there.

components.name: cropEncoder (desktopMain, injected seam)
components.responsibility: `ImageBitmap` + `DeviceRect` → PNG bytes, via skiko (`Image.makeFromBitmap(...).encodeToData()`) or `toAwtImage()`+ImageIO. Injected as a `suspend (ImageBitmap, DeviceRect) -> ByteArray?` parameter with a desktop default, exactly like the existing `decodeFrame` seam, so `commonTest` needs no real image.

components.name: RectifyWindow wiring
components.responsibility: Fills the stubbed `primaryAction` slot with the live button (`enabled = canSend`, `busy = inFlight`, `⌘↵`), adds `⌘↵` to `handleShellShortcut`, mounts the `StatusLine` and the toast, and owns the clipboard write for `Open session` (FR-58) — the host owns clipboard per `CommandBlock`'s KDoc.

alternatives.title: Publication seam A — single-slot atomic file drop under the app data dir (`~/.rectify/handoff/latest.json`)
pros: Zero new dependencies and zero IPC machinery: `Files.move(ATOMIC_MOVE)` plus `readText()`.
AC-81's idempotent 'latest' is free — the slot simply still contains the last envelope; repeated calls cannot differ.
Decoupled liveness: the payload is retrievable whether or not Rectify is running when the agent calls, which matters because the two processes have unrelated lifetimes.
Trivially testable on the desktop target with a temp dir — no sockets, no spawned process, no hardware. This is the only option that makes AC-18/AC-81 provable in the existing suite.
Atomic rename means a reader never observes a half-written envelope without any lock.
cons: Looks like the 'file fallback transport' the PRD forbids, and will have to be defended in review every time someone re-reads that sentence.
Payload bytes land on disk unencrypted. Still local-only (NFR-4 holds — no socket, no egress), but it is now at-rest data with a lifetime, which an in-memory channel would not have.
No change notification: a future `wait_for_annotations` tool would need polling or a watch service.
Needs a stale-slot policy — an envelope from last Tuesday is 'the latest' by the letter of AC-81.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Trades protocol purity and at-rest cleanliness for the smallest possible amount of code and the only end-to-end testability story available under a desktop-only test target. The PRD's prohibition reads to me as being about the agent-facing contract (the agent must call a tool, not read a folder), which this preserves exactly — the agent never learns the path.

alternatives.title: Publication seam B — AF_UNIX domain socket (JVM 21 `UnixDomainSocketAddress`), Rectify listens, the MCP server connects on each tool call
pros: Nothing is persisted; the payload lives only in the publishing process's memory.
Still literally satisfies NFR-4 — a Unix domain socket is a filesystem node, not a network socket; no port, no egress.
Natural upgrade path to a future `wait_for_annotations` push tool.
Harder to mistake for the forbidden 'file fallback transport'.
cons: Couples liveness hard: if Rectify is closed or was never started, the tool call fails instead of returning the last payload, which directly weakens AC-81's 'returns the same last-sent payload'.

Measurably more code: a listener thread/coroutine in the GUI process, connection accept/close handling, a length-prefixed frame format on top (a socket has no message boundaries), and a socket-file cleanup path for crashes.
A second concurrency surface inside the Compose app process, which currently has exactly one (`ProcessRunner`).
Testing it means standing up two endpoints in-test; still possible on desktop, but materially more fixture than a temp dir.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Cleaner on paper, more moving parts in practice, and it trades away the one property AC-81 actually asks for (the last payload is still there later). Worth revisiting the moment a push-style tool is specified — not before.

alternatives.title: Publication seam C — MCP server hosted in-process inside the Rectify JVM, with a thin spawned stdio relay
pros: The 'store' really is just an in-memory field — no serialization boundary inside the machine at all.
One source of truth for payload state.
cons: Does not remove the cross-process problem, it adds a hop: Claude Code still spawns a process, so the relay must still reach the GUI process by socket or file — strictly a superset of A or B.
Two protocol translations instead of one.
Same liveness coupling as B, plus a relay to debug.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Strictly dominated. Listed because 'just keep it in memory' is the first instinct and it needs an explicit answer: in-memory is not reachable from a process you did not start.

alternatives.title: Server location A — new plain-JVM `:mcp-application` module with its own `main()`
pros: Server classpath is `:data-handoff-api` + kotlinx-serialization only; JVM start is fast, which matters for a tool a user's agent spawns.
No conflict with `compose.desktop.application { mainClass }`, which `:desktop-application` already owns.
`installDist` gives a stable launcher path for a `.mcp.json` command entry.
Mirrors the precedent `:desktop-application` already set and documented for a non-KMP, non-convention-plugin module.
cons: A second entry point and a seventh top-level module in `settings.gradle.kts`.
No convention plugin models it — bespoke (if tiny) Gradle, which CLAUDE.md pushes back on.
Two artefacts to keep version-aligned against one envelope format.
alternatives.tradeoffs: One extra module for a clean, Compose-free server process. The bespoke-Gradle objection is real but already conceded once for `:desktop-application` on the identical grounds (convention plugins are built around `KotlinMultiplatformExtension`).

alternatives.title: Server location B — a second `main()` class inside `:desktop-application`
pros: No new module, no `settings.gradle.kts` change, nothing new for the convention-plugin rule to object to.
One build artefact to distribute.
cons: Drags all of Compose Desktop and Skiko onto the classpath of a process whose entire job is reading stdin — slow, heavy JVM start for every agent tool call.
`compose.desktop.application { mainClass }` names exactly one main; a second launcher needs its own `startScripts`/jar task, so the 'no new Gradle' advantage mostly evaporates.
Blurs a module whose own CLAUDE.md says it contains 'the single required entry point and nothing else'.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Saves a module and spends it on startup cost plus a contradicted module doc. Reasonable if the survey prefers minimum module count over process weight.

alternatives.title: Hierarchy XML source — re-serialize from parsed `HierarchySnapshotModel.nodes` instead of threading the raw dump through
pros: Touches no existing data-layer type; `HierarchySnapshotModel` keeps its current four fields.
Output is guaranteed well-formed XML, unlike the real dump (adb glues `UI hierchary dumped to: /dev/tty` onto `</hierarchy>`).
Pure function, trivially unit-testable in `commonTest`.
cons: Lossy by construction: `parseUiAutomatorDump` keeps only the attributes the measuring code needs, so every other attribute a real dump carries is gone from the payload the agent receives.
Ships a synthesised document labelled `hierarchy.xml` that is not what the device said — exactly the class of fabrication `PromptAssembly`'s KDoc refuses on three separate counts.
Grows a second XML serializer in a repo whose documented position is that it deliberately does not parse XML.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Cheaper diff, dishonest artefact. Threading the raw dump text through (one extra field on `HierarchySnapshotModel`, set by `HierarchySnapshotMapper` which already holds `stdout.dump`) costs a handful of lines and gives the agent what the device actually emitted.

exceptions: Publish failure (slot directory unwritable, disk full, permission denied): surfaces as `Failure.Technical.Platform` per error-handling.md, reduces to the failed `SendPhase`, leaves `frozen` and the staged batch intact (AS-31), re-enables the button (AC-20).

Crop encoding returns `null` for one annotation: the envelope ships the remaining crops plus the full frame rather than aborting the send. A missing crop degrades the payload; a failed send loses the batch's moment.

Frozen raw PNG bytes absent (possible only if the freeze predates this feature's retention, or a decode-without-bytes test path): the send is refused before any status animation starts — a payload with no frame is not a payload (same reasoning as `hasPayload`).

Hierarchy `Absent`/`Unavailable` (iOS, or a dump the device refused): the envelope carries an empty hierarchy field and the send proceeds. AS-29 keeps the dump Android-only, and the status step still renders because the design shows it unconditionally.

MCP server reads a slot written by a newer envelope version: reads `version`, and when it exceeds the version it knows, returns a JSON-RPC error naming both numbers rather than mis-parsing. This is precisely what AC-32 exists to enable.
MCP server reads a corrupt or truncated slot (should be impossible given ATOMIC_MOVE, but a disk can still lie): returns a tool error, never throws out of the read loop and kills the process.
Malformed JSON-RPC line on stdin: respond with a parse-error object and keep reading. One bad frame must not end the session.
stdin reaches EOF (the agent went away): the server exits 0 quietly.
edgeCases: Send with zero annotations: unreachable through the UI — `canSend` is false and `AppButton` is disabled (AC-17) — and refused again in the reducer, because `⌘↵` can fire on a path the button's disabled state does not cover.

Send while a previous send is in flight: `canSend` is false for the whole in-flight window (AC-20) and the reducer drops a second `ResolveAndSend` outright. `AppButton(busy = true)` already implies disabled, so one flag covers both affordance and guard.

Two sends racing (⌘↵ held, or a double-click landing inside one frame): same reducer guard. Orbit serialises intents through its container, so the second observes the in-flight phase and no-ops — no lock needed.

Send during a dropped stream (`MirrorSession.Lost`): the send is ALLOWED and should be. F-3's whole point is that a drop does not destroy the frozen frame or its annotations — the payload is fully assembled from already-captured data and needs no device. The status sequence renders the failure variant's first step (`Stream dropped`, `StatusStepState.Error`) while the remaining three still complete, which is exactly the design's `failed`-flag variant. `MirrorDropBanner` and `Reconnect` stay the error surface; no parallel one is introduced.

MCP server never spawned / not running when the user sends: the send still succeeds — publishing writes the slot. Nothing in AC-18 or AC-19 requires a listener to exist at send time, and this is the main reason the file slot beats a socket.
`get_latest_annotation` called before any send: returns an explicit empty result ('no annotation has been sent yet'), not an error and not a stale fabrication.
`get_latest_annotation` called twice with no send in between: returns the identical envelope — AC-81, free from the storage shape.

Payload larger than a stdio frame comfortably carries: the real risk. A 1080×2400 PNG is ~1–3 MB; base64 inflates it ~33%, and a single JSON-RPC line could exceed 4 MB. Mitigated by returning the envelope WITHOUT inline image bytes by default and letting the tool result carry file references the agent reads, or by a second tool call per image. Flagged in `risks` and `openDecisions` — do not assume one line is fine.
App quits mid-send: the slot is either the old envelope or the new one, never a blend (ATOMIC_MOVE). No cleanup, no lock file, no recovery path.

`<time>s` measurement: `TimeSource.Monotonic.markNow()` at intent receipt, elapsed read after publish returns. Monotonic, not wall clock — an NTP step or a laptop sleep mid-send must not print a negative or absurd duration. Injected as a seam in the ViewModel for testability, the way `nowMs` is in `ScreencapMirrorTransport`.
Measured time rounds to `0s` on a fast local publish: floor the display at `0.1s`, or print one decimal. A toast that claims `0s` reads as a bug even when it is the truth.
`Clear` pressed while a send is in flight: `Clear` is disabled for the same in-flight window; otherwise the envelope and the counter disagree about what was just sent.

`ResumeLive` or a device loss arriving mid-send: the send already holds its own immutable snapshot of frame bytes, crops and dump, so it completes against what the user saw. The toast count comes from that snapshot, never from live state.
Success path ordering: resume live and reset the counter only AFTER the toast's data is captured (AC-21) — reading `stagedCount` after the reset would always print `0 annotations`.
implementationSteps: 1. Retain the frozen frame's raw PNG bytes: add `frozenFrameBytes: StateFlow<ByteArray?>` to `MirrorViewModel`, set in `stageAnnotation` at the same moment `currentFrozenFrame` is set, cleared with it. No new state field in `MirrorUiState` (pixels never enter the reduced state).

2. Thread the raw hierarchy dump: add `rawDump: String = ""` to `HierarchySnapshotModel` (defaulted, so every existing construction site including `Empty` keeps compiling) and populate it in `HierarchySnapshotMapper.toModel`, which already holds `stdout.dump`.

3. Create `:data-handoff-api` (library convention plugin, kotlinx-serialization). `source/envelope/AnnotationEnvelope.kt` with `version` first; `source/handoff/AnnotationHandoff.kt` + `AnnotationHandoffReader`; `core/` for the desktopMain slot path and atomic write; `internal expect fun Module.provideAnnotationHandoff()` with desktop/android/ios actuals copying `provideDeviceSources()`. Register in `settings.gradle.kts` and in `initKoin()`'s data group.

4. Unit-test the slot in `desktopTest`: publish → read → read again returns the identical envelope (AC-81); a replaced slot returns the new one; an absent slot returns `null`; `version` survives the round trip (AC-32).

5. Add `core/send/` to `presentation-feature-mirror`: `SendPhase`, `sendSteps(phase)`, `canSend(state, inFlight)`, `toastLabel(count, seconds)`. Pure, `internal`, no Compose. Test each — this is where AC-17/AC-19/AC-20 are actually proved.

6. Add `core/send/EnvelopeAssembly`: frozen frame + raw bytes + crops + `rawDump` + effective prompt (`promptOverride ?: buildPrompt(...)`) + `PAYLOAD_FORMAT_VERSION` → `AnnotationEnvelope`. Reuse `cropWindow` for crop geometry; do not re-derive it.

7. Extend the contract: `MirrorIntent.ResolveAndSend`, `MirrorIntent.OpenSession`, `MirrorUiState.send: SendPhase`, `MirrorSideEffect.SendComplete(count, seconds)` and `MirrorSideEffect.CopySessionId(id)`. The side effects exist because only the host can show a toast and touch the clipboard — same reasoning as the shipped `MirrorSideEffect.LocateAdb`.

8. Implement the ViewModel handler with the monotonic clock seam and the injected crop encoder; wire `AnnotationHandoff` through Koin. Test: in-flight guard, zero-staged guard, success resumes live and resets the counter (AC-21), failure preserves frame and annotations (AS-31/SC-25).

9. Wire `RectifyWindow`: replace the stubbed `primaryAction` with the live button (`enabled`/`busy`/`⌘↵`), disable `Clear` while in flight, add `⌘↵` to `handleShellShortcut` beside the existing `Cmd+1/2/3` dispatch, mount `StatusLine` from `sendSteps`, host the toast, and implement the clipboard copy for `Open session` at this layer.

10. Create `:mcp-application`: `kotlin("jvm")` + `application`, dependency on `:data-handoff-api` only. `main()` = stdin read loop, JSON-RPC dispatch over three methods, stdout for frames and stderr for everything else. Test the dispatcher as a pure `String -> String` function in `test/` — no spawned process required.

11. Document the `.mcp.json` entry the user must add (command = the `installDist` launcher path), in `:mcp-application`'s README/CLAUDE.md. Generating it automatically is explicitly deferred (clarify openQuestion).

12. Cross-target compile check before declaring done: `./gradlew :presentation-feature-mirror:build :data-handoff-api:build` — `commonTest` compiles for every target, and backtick names must contain no comma and no colon (testing.md).
gaps: **The raw hierarchy XML is thrown away today.** `HierarchySnapshotMapper.toModel` calls `parseUiAutomatorDump(stdout.dump)` and keeps only the parsed nodes; `HierarchySnapshotModel` has no raw field. FR-17/AC-18 require 'view-hierarchy XML dump' in the envelope, so either the raw text is threaded through (recommended, one defaulted field) or it is re-synthesised lossily from nodes. This is not optional work and it was not visible from the PRD text.

**The frozen frame's PNG bytes are thrown away today.** `MirrorViewModel` decodes `MirrorFrame.bytes` into an `ImageBitmap` and drops the bytes. Without retaining them, F-7 would have to re-encode a decoded bitmap to produce `frame.png`. Retention is a few lines; re-encoding is a lossy, slower, desktop-only detour.

**No PNG encoder exists in `commonMain`.** `decodeToImageBitmap()` is multiplatform; there is no multiplatform encode. Per-annotation crops therefore need a desktopMain-only encoder (skiko `Image.encodeToData`, or `toAwtImage()` + ImageIO). Both are already on the desktop classpath — no new dependency — but it means crop production is structurally desktop-only, which is consistent with everything else in F-7.

**No convention plugin models a plain-JVM module.** `build-logic/convention` has `application`/`feature`/`library`/`di`, all built around `KotlinMultiplatformExtension`. `:mcp-application` therefore needs its own small `build.gradle.kts`, exactly as `:desktop-application` already does and documents. Flagging loudly per the brief: this extends an existing documented deviation rather than creating a new category, but it is still bespoke Gradle and a reviewer should see it declared, not discover it.

**No `.mcp.json` exists in this repo and nothing generates one.** The user must hand-wire the server into their Claude Code MCP config. Carried over from clarify's openQuestion; it means AC-18's end-to-end proof requires a manual setup step no test can perform.

**AC-18 and AC-81 cannot be proved end-to-end in CI.** The desktop target can test the publisher, the slot round trip, and the JSON-RPC dispatcher as pure functions — which collectively cover every line — but 'a Claude Code session calling the tool receives the payload' needs a real agent and a real spawn. Plan for a manual verification script plus the three unit layers, and say so in the AC's verification notes rather than claiming automated coverage.

**No Compose UI-test harness exists**, so AC-19's animated ordering is provable only via the pure `sendSteps` projection plus a `@Preview` pair. Same constraint F-6 hit and solved the same way (`hasPayload`, `hierarchyOutlineDisplay`).

**No session identifier exists anywhere in the codebase.** FR-58's `Open session` copies 'the current session identifier' — a grep for `sessionId` returns nothing. One has to be minted (candidate: `MirrorSession.Streaming.deviceId` + `FrozenFrame.frameId` + the send timestamp, which is also the natural primary key for the envelope and for F-9's history).

**No stale-slot policy.** An envelope published days ago is still 'latest'. Suggest stamping `sentAtMs` in the envelope and letting the tool report it, rather than inventing an expiry nobody asked for.

risks.text: The file-slot handoff is judged to violate the PRD's 'no file fallback transport' in review, forcing a late rewrite to a socket.
risks.mitigation: Settle it in the survey before plan.py, with the reading stated explicitly (the prohibition is about the agent-facing transport; the agent only ever calls an MCP tool and never learns the path). `AnnotationHandoff` is an interface precisely so the implementation behind it can become AF_UNIX without touching the ViewModel, the envelope, or the server's tool surface.

risks.text: A multi-megabyte base64 payload on one JSON-RPC stdout line exceeds what the agent's stdio reader handles, so the tool call fails for exactly the large payloads users care most about.
risks.mitigation: Default the tool result to metadata + prompt + hierarchy, with image bytes referenced rather than inlined; measure a real 1080×2400 three-annotation send before fixing the shape. Decide in the survey, not during implementation.

risks.text: The second process entry point drifts out of sync with the envelope format — a user runs an old `installDist` launcher against a newly published slot.
risks.mitigation: This is literally what AC-32 is for: the server reads `version` first and refuses a version it does not know with a message naming both numbers, rather than mis-parsing into a plausible-looking wrong answer.

risks.text: AC-18/AC-81 ship 'verified' on unit tests alone, and the first real Claude Code session finds the integration broken (wrong tool-result shape, wrong `initialize` reply, a stray stdout `println`).
risks.mitigation: One manual end-to-end run against a real Claude Code session is a required exit criterion, not a nice-to-have. Add a lint-level rule for the server module: no `println` outside the single frame writer — a stray one silently corrupts the protocol and the failure mode looks like anything but its cause.

risks.text: Retaining raw frame bytes plus per-annotation crop bitmaps grows the GUI process's heap during long sessions.
risks.mitigation: Exactly one frozen frame's bytes are retained at a time, cleared with the frame, and crops are produced during the send and released after publish — nothing accumulates. Matches the existing single-`frozenFrame` retention.

risks.text: Adding `rawDump` to `HierarchySnapshotModel` makes the model carry tens of kilobytes of text and it ends up compared by value in a hot path.
risks.mitigation: The snapshot already lives OUTSIDE the reduced state on `MirrorViewModel.frozenHierarchy` for exactly this reason, and is reduced to a four-state `HierarchyStatus` verdict. Keep it that way; do not let `rawDump` reach `MirrorUiState`.

risks.text: Clipboard write for `Open session` needs a Compose API documented as deprecated in this version (per `CommandBlock`'s KDoc), whose replacement is suspend-based.
risks.mitigation: Do it at the window layer in AWT (`Toolkit.getDefaultToolkit().systemClipboard`), which `:compose-application`'s desktopMain can reach and which is stable. This is precisely why `CommandBlock` pushed copying out to the host.

readyMadeSolutions.name: StatusLine + StatusStep/StatusStepState
readyMadeSolutions.fit: Ships FR-18/AC-19 whole. Its own `@Preview` already renders `Streaming › Frozen › Dumping hierarchy › Sent` with `trailing = "live"` AND the failure variant `Stream dropped (Error) › Frozen › …` with `trailing = "failed"`. Coloured dots, per-step state, mono labels — all present. F-7 writes a pure `SendPhase -> List<StatusStep>` projection and nothing else.

readyMadeSolutions.name: CounterBadge (Empty/Staged/Sent)
readyMadeSolutions.fit: FR-16's counter is live today. `CounterBadgeState.Sent` already exists for the post-send moment — no new state, no new component.

readyMadeSolutions.name: AppButton with `busy` (busy implies disabled) + `shortcut` affix + KeyCap
readyMadeSolutions.ref: presentation-core-ui/.../atom/button/AppButton.kt; the stub already sits at RectifyWindow.kt:304 with `shortcut = "⌘↵"`
readyMadeSolutions.fit: AC-17's disabled-at-zero and AC-20's disabled-while-in-flight are one `enabled` and one `busy` flag on a button that is already composed. The design's `⌘↩` affix is already rendering.

readyMadeSolutions.name: StackedSnackbarHost / StackedSnakbarHostState
readyMadeSolutions.fit: Hosts the completion toast with its `Open session` action (FR-18/FR-58) without inventing a Toast component. `FeedbackBar` is the alternative if the design wants an inline outcome bar rather than a floating one.

readyMadeSolutions.name: `expect fun Module.provideDeviceSources()` + `UnsupportedDeviceSources` pattern
readyMadeSolutions.fit: The exact, already-proven shape for binding a desktop-only implementation into a commonMain Koin graph while Android/iOS still link. Copy it for `provideAnnotationHandoff()` instead of inventing a desktop-only DI path.

readyMadeSolutions.name: F-6's `buildPrompt` and `cropWindow`
readyMadeSolutions.fit: The envelope's prompt text and crop geometry are already computed, tested, and documented down to why there is no `measured:` branch. F-7 consumes both; it rebuilds neither.

readyMadeSolutions.name: F-3's MirrorDropBanner / Reconnect / canResumeLive
readyMadeSolutions.fit: The send-failure surface. AS-31 preserves the frozen frame and the batch exactly as an involuntary drop does, so a failed send reuses the shipped error affordances rather than growing a parallel set.

readyMadeSolutions.name: kotlinx-serialization (cataloged, in use)
readyMadeSolutions.fit: Covers both the envelope and the JSON-RPC frames. With `readLine()`/`println` as the framing, no MCP SDK and no `ktor-server-*` entry are needed — and neither exists in the catalog today.

readyMadeSolutions.name: `decodeFrame` / `nowMs` injected-seam precedent
readyMadeSolutions.fit: Exactly how the crop encoder and the elapsed-time clock should enter the ViewModel, so `commonTest` needs neither a real image nor real wall-clock time. Note `ScreencapMirrorTransport`'s Koin binding is `single<T> { … }` and NOT `singleOf` precisely so a defaulted seam survives — the same trap applies here.

readyMadeSolutions.name: `CommandBlock.onCopy` host-owns-clipboard precedent
readyMadeSolutions.fit: Its KDoc already states that Compose's `ClipboardManager` is deprecated in this version and that copying belongs to the host. FR-58 follows the same route: a side effect up to `RectifyWindow`, which does the AWT clipboard write.

readyMadeSolutions.name: `ProcessRunner`'s concurrent-drain / timeout lessons
readyMadeSolutions.fit: The server reads stdin and writes stdout in one process, so it does not need `ProcessRunner` — but its two documented hazards transfer directly: never block on one stream while the other fills, and never let a `withTimeout` cancellation be swallowed by a `Throwable` catch.

techStack.choice: kotlinx-serialization JSON, `@Serializable` data class with `version: Int` as the first field
techStack.reason: Already cataloged and in use; no new dependency (NFR-15). The explicit version field is AC-32 and NFR-12 in one line.
Settled in clarify Q3. No socket is ever opened, so NFR-4 is literally true rather than argued.

techStack.choice: Hand-rolled over kotlinx-serialization (~3 methods), no SDK
techStack.reason: The brief asks for the hand-rolled path to be justified: serialization is already solved by a cataloged library, and the remaining surface is `initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call` plus `readLine()`/`println` framing. There is no MCP SDK and no JSON-RPC library in `libs.versions.toml`; adding either to avoid ~120 lines is the bigger decision. Revisit if the deferred hardening (multi-client, auth, discovery) lands.

techStack.choice: Single-slot JSON file under `~/.rectify/handoff/`, written with `Files.move(ATOMIC_MOVE, REPLACE_EXISTING)`
techStack.reason: `java.nio.file` only; atomic rename removes the need for a lock; a re-read is AC-81's idempotency for free.

techStack.choice: Reuse the original `MirrorFrame.bytes` captured by `adb screencap -p`
techStack.reason: Already PNG-encoded upstream; retaining it avoids a decode/re-encode round trip entirely.

techStack.choice: skiko `Image.makeFromBitmap(...).encodeToData()` (or `toAwtImage()` + ImageIO), desktopMain only, injected as a seam
techStack.reason: Both are already on the desktop classpath via Compose Desktop — no new dependency. Injected so `commonTest` needs no real image, matching `decodeFrame`.
Wall clock can step backwards (NTP, sleep) and would print a nonsense `<time>s`. Monotonic cannot; injection makes it testable.
No convention plugin models a plain-JVM module. `:desktop-application` already set and documented this precedent; `installDist` gives the `.mcp.json` a stable command path.

techStack.choice: Koin, `internal expect fun Module.provideAnnotationHandoff()` with per-platform actuals
techStack.reason: Verbatim reuse of `data-device-impl`'s `provideDeviceSources()` shape, including the Android/iOS `Unsupported*` actual that keeps every target linking.
Every piece the design calls for is already in the kit and in the registry. F-7 adds pure projections, not components.

openDecisions.decision: Does `get_latest_annotation` inline base64 image bytes in the tool result, or return metadata plus references the agent fetches separately?
options: Inline everything in one JSON-RPC response
Metadata + prompt + hierarchy inline, images by reference
Inline, with a size ceiling that degrades to reference above it
openDecisions.recommendation: Metadata + prompt + hierarchy inline, images by reference — measure a real three-annotation 1080×2400 send before committing, since a multi-megabyte single line is the most likely integration failure.
openDecisions.resolution: Metadata + prompt + hierarchy inline, images by reference — settled at the Stage 1 brainstorm human gate. Measure a real three-annotation 1080x2400 send during implementation to confirm the inline portion stays small.

openDecisions.decision: What composes the session identifier FR-58 copies? Nothing in the codebase has one today.
options: deviceId + frameId + sentAtMs
A random UUID minted per send
The envelope's slot filename
openDecisions.recommendation: deviceId + frameId + sentAtMs — derived from data that already exists, human-readable when pasted, and the natural primary key for F-9's history.

openDecisions.decision: Is a stale published slot (hours or days old) still a valid `get_latest_annotation` answer?
options: Yes, unconditionally — 'latest' means latest
Yes, but the result reports `sentAtMs` so the agent can judge
No — expire after N minutes
openDecisions.recommendation: Report `sentAtMs` and let the agent judge. An expiry is a policy nobody asked for, and AC-81's wording is unconditional.

survey.question: CRUX — The MCP server is a separate process Claude Code spawns. How does the UI hand its versioned payload to the server?
options: Single-slot atomic file drop under the app data dir (~/.rectify/handoff/latest.json, temp-write + ATOMIC_MOVE); the server re-reads it on each tool call
AF_UNIX domain socket (JVM 21 UnixDomainSocketAddress)
MCP server hosted in-process inside Rectify with a thin spawned stdio relay
survey.answer: Single-slot atomic file drop under the app data dir (~/.rectify/handoff/latest.json, temp-write + ATOMIC_MOVE); the server re-reads it on each tool call

survey.question: Where does the MCP server's main() live?

A second main class inside :desktop-application
Inside :compose-application's desktopMain
